methods.name: CAT structural MRI VBM and SBM analysis
methods.purpose: Measure brain structure in T1-weighted MRI scans at voxel, region, and cortical surface levels, including thickness and folding, with quality control and statistics built in.

inputs.statement: T1-weighted MRI scans, single scans, longitudinal series or BIDS datasets
inputs.quote:
T1-weighted MRI
Single scans, longitudinal series or BIDS datasets

conditions.statement: For MATLAB users, SPM12 or newer and MATLAB R2020a or newer are required; no additional MATLAB toolboxes are needed.
conditions.quote:
SPM12 or newer
MATLAB R2020a or newer (Windows: R2022a, Apple Silicon: R2023b)
No additional MATLAB toolboxes

conditions.statement: Standalone version runs with MATLAB Runtime R2023b and is mainly intended for scripted, headless use on servers and clusters; some features like parallelization and interactive help are not available.
conditions.quote: Runs with the free MATLAB Runtime R2023b (v232) and is mainly intended for scripted, headless use on servers and clusters. Some features, such as parallelization and the interactive help, are not available.

steps.statement: Install CAT by copying it into SPM's toolbox folder, or use the standalone version without MATLAB.
steps.quote: Copy CAT into SPM’s toolbox folder, or use the standalone version without MATLAB.

steps.statement: Preprocess: select T1 images or a BIDS dataset and run Segment; CAT processes subjects in parallel.
steps.quote: Select your T1 images or a BIDS dataset and run Segment. CAT processes subjects in parallel.

steps.statement: Check quality: review each scan's report and rating, and check sample homogeneity to catch outliers.
steps.quote: Review each scan’s report and rating, and check sample homogeneity to catch outliers.

steps.statement: Analyze: run voxel-, ROI- or surface-based statistics and show results on slices or on the cortical surface.
steps.quote: Run voxel-, ROI- or surface-based statistics and show results on slices or on the cortical surface.

checks.statement: Every scan gets a one-page report with tissue volumes, surface measures and image-quality ratings; noise, bias and resolution are combined into a grade from A (excellent) to F (failed).
checks.quote: Every scan gets a one-page report with tissue volumes, surface measures and image-quality ratings. Noise, bias and resolution are combined into one grade from A (excellent) to F (failed)

checks.statement: A sample homogeneity check flags outliers before statistics.
checks.quote: Sample homogeneity check flags outliers before statistics

exceptions.statement: The standalone version lacks some features such as parallelization and interactive help.
exceptions.quote: Some features, such as parallelization and the interactive help, are not available.

outputs.statement: Voxel-based morphometry outputs modulated tissue maps ready for statistics in SPM, total intracranial volume (TIV) and global tissue volumes.
outputs.quote:
Modulated tissue maps, ready for statistics in SPM
Total intracranial volume (TIV) and global tissue volumes

outputs.statement: Region-based morphometry outputs regional tissue volumes and regional surface values (thickness, folding or mapped data), ready to export as CSV.
outputs.quote: you get regional tissue volumes and regional surface values (thickness, folding or mapped data), ready to export as CSV.

outputs.statement: Surface-based morphometry outputs cortical thickness, folding measures (gyrification, sulcal depth, cortical complexity), and surface area.
outputs.quote:
Cortical thickness
Folding: gyrification, sulcal depth and cortical complexity (fractal dimension)
New Surface area

outputs.statement: Quality control outputs an automatic quality rating (SIQR) for every scan and a sample homogeneity check.
outputs.quote:
Automatic quality rating (SIQR) for every scan
Sample homogeneity check flags outliers before statistics

parameters.statement: Registration can use Dartel or Geodesic Shooting to templates in MNI152NLin2009cAsym space.
parameters.quote: Dartel (Ashburner 2007) or Geodesic Shooting (Ashburner 2011) to templates in MNI152NLin2009cAsym space.

parameters.statement: Spherical registration to standard 164k or 32k (HCP) meshes is available for group statistics.
parameters.quote: Spherical registration to standard 164k or 32k (HCP) meshes for group statistics

parameters.statement: Surface mapping can sample at chosen cortical depths (equi-distance or equi-volume).
parameters.quote: Sampling at chosen cortical depths (equi-distance or equi-volume)

methods.name: FSL-VBM
methods.purpose: Voxel-wise investigation of local grey matter volume/topography differences between populations or related to a clinical score, following the optimised VBM protocol.

inputs.statement: A template_list file containing the names of selected T1 images to be used for template construction, with equal numbers from each group.
inputs.quote: put all the selected names of exams in a file called template_list in your FSL-VBM directory

inputs.statement: design.mat and design.con files specifying the cross-subject statistical model, with row order matching the image order from imglob.
inputs.quote: create your design.mat and design.con in your FSL-VBM directory; see the randomise manual

inputs.statement: A GM mask (GM_mask) and the 4D multi-subject concatenated processed data (e.g., GM_mod_merg_s3) for running randomise.
inputs.quote: a mask of the GM (GM_mask) and the 4D multi-subject concatenated processed data (e.g. GM_mod_merg_s3)

conditions.statement: All different populations included in the study must be represented in the template construction.
conditions.quote: All your different populations included in this study MUST be represented in the template construction.

conditions.statement: Use the same number of subjects from each group in the template construction to avoid bias in non-linear registration.
conditions.quote: You should use the same number of subjects from each in the construction of the study-specific template.

conditions.statement: The order of rows in design.mat must match the order of images when doing imglob * in the FSL-VBM directory.
conditions.quote: The order of the rows in your design.mat model MUST match the order of your images when doing an imglob * command

steps.statement: Run fslvbm_1_bet with -b or -N option to perform brain extraction on all T1 images.
steps.quote:
fslvbm_1_bet -b
or
fslvbm_1_bet -N

steps.statement: Run fslvbm_2_template with -a or -n option to create the study-specific symmetric grey matter template.
steps.quote:
fslvbm_2_template -a
or
fslvbm_2_template -n

steps.statement: Run fslvbm_3_proc to non-linearly register all GM images to the template, modulate, smooth, and run an initial GLM for qualitative evaluation.
steps.quote: fslvbm_3_proc

steps.statement: Choose the most appropriate smoothing (e.g., sigma=3mm) and optionally apply a different smoothing with fslmaths.
steps.quote: fslmaths GM_mod_merg -s 3.5 GM_mod_merg_s3.5

steps.statement: Run randomise with TFCE or cluster-based thresholding for permutation-based inference.
steps.quote: randomise -i GM_mod_merg_s3 -m GM_mask -o fslvbm -d design.mat -t design.con -T -n 5000

steps.statement: Display results in FSLView/FSLeyes overlaid on the MNI152 template or template_GM.
steps.quote: fsleyes $FSLDIR/data/standard/MNI152_T1_2mm fslvbm_tfce_corrp_tstat1 -cm red-yellow -dr 0.949 1

steps.statement: For cluster-based results, threshold corrected p-value maps at 0.95 and mask the tstat map before display.
steps.quote: fslmaths fslvbm_clustere_corrp_tstat1 -thr 0.95 -bin mask_pcorrected

checks.statement: Check brain-extracted images (*_brain.*) in the struc directory after fslvbm_1_bet.
checks.quote: CHECKING the brain images (*_brain.*) in your struc directory

checks.statement: Check the template_GM_4D image in struc with the movie loop in fsleyes after template creation.
checks.quote: CHECK the template_GM_4D image in struc with the movie loop in fsleyes.

checks.statement: Check the 4D image of modulated registered GM images (GM_mod_merg) using the movie loop in fsleyes after fslvbm_3_proc.
checks.quote: final CHECK of the 4D image of modulated registered GM images GM_mod_merg using the movie loop in fsleyes.

exceptions.statement: FSL-VBM v1.1 analysis is not compatible with an older analysis due to the switch from IRTK to FNIRT.
exceptions.quote: An FSL-VBM v1.1 analysis is not compatible with an older analysis.

outputs.statement: Study-specific symmetric grey matter template (template_GM) at 2x2x2mm3 resolution in standard space.
outputs.quote: final symmetric, study-specific "non-linear" GM template at 2x2x2mm3 resolution in standard space.

outputs.statement: 4D image of modulated registered GM images (GM_mod_merg) in the stats directory.
outputs.quote: All the modulated registered GM images are concatenated into a 4D image in the stats directory (GM_mod_merg)

outputs.statement: Smoothed modulated GM images (e.g., GM_mod_merg_s3) for various Gaussian kernels.
outputs.quote: smoothed (GM_mod_merg_s3 for instance) by a range of Gaussian kernels; sigma = 2, 3, 4mm

parameters.statement: Smoothing kernel sigma values of 2, 3, and 4 mm are applied by default in fslvbm_3_proc.
parameters.quote: sigma = 2, 3, 4mm, i.e., approximately from FWHM = 2x2.3 = 4.6mm to FWHM = 9mm.

parameters.statement: Non-linear registration uses free-form deformation with 20 mm initial control point spacing.
parameters.quote: free-form deformation with 20 mm initial control point spacing

parameters.statement: For TFCE-based randomise, a typical number of permutations is 5000.
parameters.quote: randomise -i GM_mod_merg_s3 -m GM_mask -o fslvbm -d design.mat -t design.con -T -n 5000

parameters.statement: For cluster-based thresholding, a typical cluster-forming threshold is t > 2.3.
parameters.quote: threshold (e.g. t > 2.3) for the cluster-based correction

methods.name: FreeSurfer Local Gyrification Index (lGI)
methods.purpose: Compute local gyrification index, a metric quantifying the amount of cortex buried within sulcal folds compared with outer visible cortex, at each vertex of the pial surface.

inputs.statement: The pial surface file (?h.pial) for the subject, produced by the recon-all -all stream.
inputs.quote: usage of the -localGI feature assumes that a subject has already been processed by the freesurfer {{{recon-all -s <subjid> -all}}} stream, such that the ?h.pial surface files exist

inputs.statement: The subject's surf directory containing the pial surface files.
inputs.quote: such that the ?h.pial surface files exist in the subject's <subj>/surf directory

inputs.statement: MATLAB with Image Processing Toolbox and $FREESURFER_HOME/matlab in the MATLAB path.
inputs.quote: MATLAB is required to use the -localGI feature. Also, you will need their Image Processing Toolbox.

conditions.statement: The subject must have been processed with the full recon-all stream before using -localGI.
conditions.quote: usage of the -localGI feature assumes that a subject has already been processed by the freesurfer {{{recon-all -s <subjid> -all}}} stream

conditions.statement: MATLAB and its Image Processing Toolbox must be installed and accessible.
conditions.quote: MATLAB is required to use the -localGI feature. Also, you will need their Image Processing Toolbox.

conditions.statement: The MATLAB path must include $FREESURFER_HOME/matlab, set up in ~/matlab/startup.m.
conditions.quote: You will also need $FREESURFER_HOME/matlab in your matlab path set up in your ~/matlab/starup.m script.

steps.statement: Run recon-all with the -localGI flag to compute the local gyrification index.
steps.quote:
In freesurfer, use the -localGI flag of recon-all:
recon-all -s <subj> -localGI

steps.statement: Create an outer smoothed surface by morphological closing of the pial surface using mris_fill and make_outer_surface with a spherical structural element.
steps.quote: an 'outer surface' surface file is created, called ?h.outer-pial-smoothed, which is basically an 'enveloped' version of the (pial) input. It is created by a morphological closing operation

steps.statement: Extract the main component and smooth the outer surface using mris_extract_main_component and mris_smooth.
steps.quote:
?h.pial-outer-main
mris_smooth -nw -n 30
?h.pial-outer-smoothed

steps.statement: Convert the outer smoothed surface to ASCII normals using mris_convert.
steps.quote:
?h.pial-outer-smoothed
mris_convert -n (output normals as ascii)
?h.pial-outer-smoothed-normals.asc

steps.statement: Find corresponding centers between pial and outer smoothed surfaces using find_corresponding_center_FSformat.
steps.quote:
?h.pial, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed
find_corresponding_center_FSformat
?h.pial.*.center

steps.statement: Define circular regions of interest on the outer surface using make_roi_paths in MATLAB.
steps.quote:
?h.pial, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed.asc
make_roi_paths
?h.pial.*.path

steps.statement: Convert paths to labels using mri_path2label.
steps.quote:
?h.pial.*.path, ?h.pial.*.center
mri_path2label
?h.pial.*.label

steps.statement: Compute lGI values using compute_lgi in MATLAB and convert the result to the final surface file with mris_convert.
steps.quote:
?h.pial, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed-normals.asc, ?h.pial.*.labels, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed-mesh
compute_lgi
?h.pial_lgi.asc

checks.statement: Check for topological defects of the pial surface using mris_euler_number, as defects cause mris_compute_lgi to crash.
checks.quote: In case of topological defects of the pial surface (run mris_euler_number), mris_compute_lgi crashes.

exceptions.statement: If mris_compute_lgi crashes due to topological defects, simply relaunching it is usually sufficient to overcome the issue.
exceptions.quote: Usually, simply relaunching mris_compute_lgi is sufficient to overcome this issue.

outputs.statement: Files named lh.pial_lgi and rh.pial_lgi in the subject's surf directory, containing lGI values at each vertex of the pial surface.
outputs.quote: This will produce files named lh.pial_lgi and rh.pial_lgi in the subjects surf directory.

outputs.statement: The primary output file ?h.pial_lgi can be viewed as an overlay in tksurfer or freeview.
outputs.quote: The primary output file is ?h.pial_lgi, which can be viewed as an overlay in tksurfer or freeview

outputs.statement: The output can be used for vertex-wise analysis in QDEC after sampling to fsaverage.
outputs.quote: To perform a vertex-wise analysis in QDEC of the lgi surface data, first sample the results to the average template subject 'fsaverage'

outputs.statement: ROI-based statistics can be generated using mri_segstats with the pial_lgi file.
outputs.quote:
It is also possible to generate statistics on ROIs, for example:
mri_segstats --annot my_subject_id lh aparc --i $SUBJECTS_DIR/my_subject_id/surf/lh.pial_lgi --sum lh.aparc.pial_lgi.stats

parameters.statement: Diameter of the structural element sphere used in morphological closing; decreasing below 10mm produces an outer surface entering sulci, increasing does not substantially affect morphology but increases computation time.
parameters.quote: Decreasing the diameter of the se sphere below 10mm will produce an outer surface entering in the sulci. Increasing it does not substantially affect the morphology of the outer surfaces (but increase computation time!).

parameters.statement: Number of smoothing iterations for mris_smooth is set to 30.
parameters.quote: mris_smooth -nw -n 30

parameters.statement: The structural element size for make_outer_surface is set to 15.
parameters.quote: make_outer_surface -se 15

methods.name: CIVET-Macaque cortical surface reconstruction and quality controls
methods.purpose: Automated extraction of cortical surfaces and evaluation of cortical thickness from macaque T1-weighted MR images, with surface-based registration and quality controls.

inputs.statement: T1-weighted MR scan of a macaque brain as the primary input.
inputs.quote: CIVET takes as input a T1w scan and registers if to standardized space, herein the NMT

inputs.statement: Optional T2-weighted or proton density scans for multimodal tissue classification.
inputs.quote: with the possibility of a multimodal classification should T2-weighted and/or proton density scans be available

inputs.statement: NMT brain mask and tissue priors for registration and classification.
inputs.quote: Registration, using minctracc, proceeds by specifying the brain mask on the target image only, herein the NMT volume with its associated brain mask

conditions.statement: The pipeline is designed for macaque brains and uses a length scale of 0.4 relative to human brain size.
conditions.quote: A length scale of 0.4 was derived from the cubic root of the macaque-to-human volume ratio

conditions.statement: Processing is performed in the NMT standardized space.
conditions.quote: Processing is performed based on the NIMH Macaque Template (NMT), as the reference template

conditions.statement: The pipeline requires T1w scans; T2-weighted or proton density scans are optional for multimodal classification.
conditions.quote: relies on the T1w scan, with the possibility of a multimodal classification should T2-weighted and/or proton density scans be available

conditions.statement: The NMT v2 is the current version of the template, with symmetric and asymmetric variants and multiple resolutions.
conditions.quote: The NMT v2 is the most current version of this dataset.

steps.statement: Resample the image into NMT space at 0.25 or 0.50 mm isotropic resolution.
steps.quote: The macaque brain is resampled in linear standardized space at the processing voxel resolution of 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm

steps.statement: Mask the brain using FSL bet with intensities sampled within the template brain mask.
steps.quote: Brain-masking is based on extensions of FSL bet version 1 (Smith, 2002) and is applied in standardized space

steps.statement: Classify the brain into CSF, gray matter, and white matter using an artificial neural network trained on tissue priors.
steps.quote: The brain is classified into cerebrospinal fluid, gray matter, and white matter using an artificial neural network (ANN) trained on the intensities of the tissue priors

steps.statement: Mask blood vessels by detecting T1w hyperintensities with line morphology in sulci.
steps.quote: it is critical to identify T1w hyperintensities, commonly representing major blood vessels and erroneously segmented as white matter by the classifier

steps.statement: Perform surface-based registration to the average surface template and resample cortical thickness maps.
steps.quote: Surface-based registration is performed and the cortical thickness maps are blurred and resampled at the common vertex locations of the template

checks.statement: Quality control includes visual inspection of brain masks and surfaces for accuracy.
checks.quote: The procedure proved to be very robust at extracting accurate masks on scans of individual subjects (see Fig. 2)

checks.statement: The N3 spline distance should be empirically determined to ensure uniform gray and white matter intensities.
checks.quote: This value can be determined empirically such that the intensities for gray matter and white matter appear mostly uniform across the brain.

exceptions.statement: The pipeline is not validated for species other than macaques; adaptations for other primates would require appropriate length scales and templates.
exceptions.quote: Further adaptations of the pipeline to other non-human primate brains should be straightforward by introducing the appropriate length scales and supplying species specific templates.

exceptions.statement: The NMT v2 is the current version; the paper describes NMT v1.2, so users should be aware of version differences.
exceptions.quote: The NMT v2 is the most current version of this dataset.

exceptions.statement: The pipeline may require manual intervention for custom brain masks in rare registration failures.
exceptions.quote: In the rare case when registration fails, a custom brain mask in native space can be supplied.

outputs.statement: Cortical thickness maps calculated as the distance between the two cortical surfaces.
outputs.quote: Cortical thickness is calculated as the distance between the two cortical surfaces.

outputs.statement: Surface-based registration results with resampled cortical thickness maps at template vertex locations.
outputs.quote: Surface-based registration is performed and the cortical thickness maps are blurred and resampled at the common vertex locations of the template

outputs.statement: Outputs can be exported in NIfTI/GIfTI formats for integration with other tools.
outputs.quote: Full compatibility exists to read input T1w scans in NIfTI format and to export the outputs in the commonly used NIfTI/GIfTI formats

parameters.statement: Length scale of 0.4 for all length-related parameters relative to human brain size.
parameters.quote: A length scale of 0.4 was derived from the cubic root of the macaque-to-human volume ratio

parameters.statement: Processing voxel resolution of 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm.
parameters.quote: The macaque brain is resampled in linear standardized space at the processing voxel resolution of 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm

methods.name: Macapype NHP anatomical processing pipeline
methods.purpose: Process nonhuman primate (NHP) brain MRI data in BIDS format, including data preparation, brain extraction, and brain segmentation, with optional template-based processing and derivatives output.
methods.species_scope: macaque, marmoset, baboon, chimpanzee (as supported by -species option)

inputs.statement: Input data must be in BIDS format, with T1w and T2w images expected.
inputs.quote: All the data have to be in BIDS format to run properly

inputs.statement: T1 weighted images are expected with the _T1w BIDS extension.
inputs.quote: _T1w (BIDS) extension is expected for T1 weighted images

inputs.statement: T2 weighted images are expected with the _T2w BIDS extension.
inputs.quote: _T2w (BIDS) extension is expected for T2 weighted images

inputs.statement: All files with the same extension (T1w or T2w) will be aligned to the first one and averaged.
inputs.quote: All files with the same extension (T1w or T2w) will be aligned to the first one and averaged

conditions.statement: The -data parameter must point to an existing BIDS format directory.
conditions.quote: -data : path to your data dataset (existing BIDS format directory)

conditions.statement: The -out parameter must point to an existing output path.
conditions.quote: -out : path to the output results (an existing path)

conditions.statement: The -soft parameter must be either SPM or ANTS, with SPM requiring a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d not available by default.
conditions.quote: -soft : can be one of these : SPM or ANTS ( NB: SPM requires a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d, not available by default)

conditions.statement: Either -params or -species must be provided; -params is mandatory if -species is omitted, and vice versa.
conditions.quote: -params : (mandatory if -species is omitted) a json file specifiying the global parameters of the analysis.

steps.statement: Run the main script segment_pnh.py as a Python script, or use the segment_pnh command if installed via pypi or container.
steps.quote:
The main file is located in workflows and is called segment_pnh.py and should be called like a python script:
$ python workflows/segment_pnh.py

steps.statement: Specify the input data directory, output directory, and software choice (SPM or ANTS) as mandatory command line parameters.
steps.quote:
-data : path to your data dataset (existing BIDS format directory)
-out : path to the output results (an existing path)
-soft : can be one of these : SPM or ANTS

steps.statement: Provide either a -params JSON file with global parameters or a -species option specifying the NHP species (e.g., macaque, marmo, baboon, chimp).
steps.quote:
-params : (mandatory if -species is omitted) a json file specifiying the global parameters of the analysis. See Parameters for more details
-species : (mandatory if -params is omitted) followed the NHP species corresponding to the image, e.g. {macaque | marmo | baboon | chimp}

steps.statement: Optionally specify the datatype for brain segmentation using -dt, which can be 'T1' or 'T1 T2'; default is T1 if omitted.
steps.quote:

metadata.purpose: Identify cortical reconstruction failures and determine appropriate quality control and repair stages in the FreeSurfer recon-all pipeline.
